summary_paragraph: A woman with Roux-en-Y gastric bypass and gastrostomy tube dependence was directly admitted for recurrent worsening epigastric band-like abdominal pain radiating to the left flank shortly after a recent discharge for suspected ulcer-related pain despite adherence to PPI and sucralfate. Evaluation showed stable vital signs, reassuring labs without leukocytosis or pancreatitis, and CT abdomen/pelvis with contrast demonstrating no fluid collection or intra-abdominal phlegmon with only expected postoperative scarring. She was managed conservatively with IV fluids, antacid/ulcer therapy continuation, tube feeds switched to Vivonex with good tolerance, antiemetics, and analgesia transitioned from IV morphine to oral hydromorphone and acetaminophen. Significant bloating and pain improved after bowel regimen including a Fleet enema with large bowel movement. She was discharged home ambulatory and stable, tolerating tube feeds, with return precautions and surgical follow-up.
problems: Major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified
